purpose: Candidate real-world bad items for BLIND testing. They must not be used to tune rules. Each needs a public source; verification level is recorded honestly.

categories.malicious: Intentionally harmful code or content (backdoor, exfiltration, poisoning). The static screen is meant to catch these.
categories.vulnerable: Honest code with an exploitable flaw (CVE). Needs dependency and flaw analysis, a different detector than the screen.

items.summary: Package modified from 1.0.16 to add a hidden BCC copying every outbound email to an external address. Removed from npm by 2025-09-25.
items.verification: source page fetched; timeline, versions and the one-line diff read. The Hacker News article seen in search only.
items.testable: reconstruction only: package is gone from npm. Rebuild a fixture from the one-line diff published by Snyk and label it reconstructed.
items.expected_screen_behaviour: Likely MISSED: the exfil target is a hard-coded email address (Bcc), not a URL host, so the current egress rule does not see it.

findings: Only 1 of 5 leads is a confirmed malicious MCP incident, and its package is no longer downloadable.
Real 'bad' items are mostly CVEs (vulnerable), which the static screen is not designed to detect. The screen and a vulnerability scanner must be reported separately.
Need at least 10 verified items per category before reporting a real AUC; currently 0 testable.
